title: Theater Five
paragraphs: ABC weekday anthology of short original radio dramas across crime, science fiction, suspense, social issues and other genres.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: ABC weekday anthology run (August 3, 1964 to July 30, 1965) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Fred Foy (announcer and director), Glenn Osser (conductor, performer, and composer), Jack C. Wilson (performer, script editor, and preparer), Alexander Vlas-Daczenco (composer, conductor, and performer), Ted Bell (director, producer, and executive producer), Ed Blainey (performer and sound technician), and Lee Bowman (executive producer and performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], [[org|org.5e0945ef3ae9902a|WLS-FM]], [[org|org.2291591a8979b4ab|WLS]], and [[org|org.0207d811941f7fb5|KGO]].

The stories often return to youth and juvenile conflict, family and domestic crisis, crime and criminal investigation, war and military conflict, psychological tension and mental states, and science fiction and speculative technology.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Mid-1960s network-radio drama revival effort, Contemporary social issues in mid-1960s anthology drama, and Civil-rights-era social conflict.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]], [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], and [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]].
